Earlier this year in March, Apple announced it would discontinue the Mac Pro and confirmed there are no plans to release new Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg today published a new report shedding further light on Apple's Mac Pro strategy, revealing a surprising detail about a project Apple had once developed...

The inside story of Apple shelving its Mac Pro plans

In the latest edition of his "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman explained that internally, "discontinuing the Mac Pro was not always the plan." Gurman reiterated a point from earlier reports: Apple's original idea was to launch a chip called "Extreme" on top of the "Ultra" chip.

The report noted: "Apple was said to have developed M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately shelved these projects due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the actual Mac Pro hardware development, Gurman said Apple had two models (codenamed J170 and J190) in development, but they were ultimately never released to the market.

Perhaps the most striking detail in the report is that one of the two models used an Intel processor:

Apple eventually discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removing it from its official website and directing buyers to the Mac Studio. Although this outcome had long been foreshadowed, for supporters of Mac Pro hardware, it still marks the bittersweet end of an era.

What do you think about Apple's decision to shut down the Mac Pro product line without releasing an "Extreme" chip during the Apple Silicon era? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
